admitted: The ledgerlite Ledger class has a close(name) method in src/ledgerlite/__init__.py. It raises ValueError when the account balance is not zero, and otherwise deletes the account.
Running `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from the ledgerlite project root runs the unit tests and reported Ran 2 tests, OK.
tools/check.py reads the NOTES_HOME environment variable with os.environ["NOTES_HOME"], so running the project checks requires NOTES_HOME to be set.
fieldnotes export prints each stored note as `created: text`, with `created` printed unchanged from store.load(), the same value that fieldnotes list prints.
fieldnotes list prints each stored note's 'created' value unchanged; store.add writes that value with datetime.isoformat() in UTC, so list output is ISO-8601 only for notes written through store.add.
Every date fieldnotes prints must be ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD...). Locale formats such as 'Jan 2' or '02/01/2026' must never be used.
For household planning, the user decided to keep the grocery budget under $600 per month and to have anything that would push it over flagged.
Ledger.transfer in src/ledgerlite/__init__.py calls money.parse(amount) in place of its own Decimal conversion and positivity check, and imports money from the package.

src/ledgerlite/money.py defines parse(value) that returns a finite positive Decimal, raises TypeError for types other than str or Decimal, and raises ValueError for invalid, non-finite or non-positive amounts.
